items.q: How can someone else's stress affect your body?
items.a: Tara Swart says **cortisol leaks out of sweat about an arm's length** and enters nearby skin. Hierarchy amplifies it: juniors feel drained after meetings with stressed seniors, even when leaders try to hide it.

items.q: Why does chronic stress create stubborn belly fat?
items.a: As a **survival mechanism**, elevated cortisol **stores fat around the abdomen**. Exercise and diet alone won't shift that belly fat until **chronic cortisol drops**.

items.q: Why is a stressed manager an org-health problem?
items.a: Promoting a **"cortisol-leaking" manager** damages the team below them. Leadership stress management is a **team health intervention**, not just self-care. Fixes include aerobic exercise (sweat cortisol out), journaling, therapy, and trusted conversation.

Gaze your partner's **left eye with your right eye** — that path hits the **amygdala loop** for maximum oxytocin resonance. Touch, laughter, shared struggle, and warm baths also boost bonding chemistry.
Yes in Swart's framing: co-sleeping supports **HRV resilience**, and even a partner's goodbye kiss can spike it. Hormones can also **synchronize via sweat proximity** in cohabiting groups.

items.q: How much sleep does the glymphatic system need to flush brain waste?
items.a: Ideal is about **8h15**. The glymphatic system actively flushes **tau and amyloid over 7–8 hours**; **side-sleeping** optimizes flow. Keeping sleep/wake within ~1 hour also helps.

items.q: Can your brain still change after age 25?
items.a: The brain grows actively until ~**25**, but from **25 to 65+** you can still improve executive function if challenges are **attention-intense** enough — new language, instrument, DJing — not just casual daily podcasts.

items.q: What are Swart's four steps for habit change?
items.a: **Raised awareness** (half the battle), **focused attention** (trigger → consequence), **deliberate practice**, then **accountability** via action boards — not vision boards.
In the cited study, people who only **visualized lifting for 2 weeks** (no weights) still saw about a **13% increase in muscle mass**.

items.q: Why do you keep attracting the same relationship patterns?
items.a: You meet people at your **level of psychological evolution** — and at the level of your **psychological wounds**. Values attract values; wounds attract wounds. Partner lists only work if you **embody** those values.

items.q: Should you biohack before fixing sleep and stress?
items.a: No. **Foundations before biohacks**: intermittent fasting only helps if **sleep, hydration, gentle exercise, and stress** are already managed. Affirmations should hit real beliefs ("I'm safe") over shallow ones.
